cycles.theme: God made a good world and remains present, powerful, and caring within His story.
The Bible is one connected story of the faithful God making and keeping His promises.
God sees people in danger and sin, provides rescue, and calls His people to trust Him.
God is the true King, human rulers fail, and Jesus rules through truth, service, the cross, and resurrection.
God forms a people who worship, learn, serve, forgive, share, and carry the good news together.
Students construct a reliable whole-Bible timeline and learn to read individual passages inside one connected story.
Students learn how covenant, kingship, wisdom, worship, prophecy, and exile deepen the Bible's central story.
Students study Jesus through the Gospels, understand the gospel response, and practise reading Jesus' teaching in context.
Students examine the church in Acts and the Epistles, learn how Christians reason from Scripture, and locate church life within resurrection hope.
Students consolidate the biblical metanarrative while learning observation, context, genre, translation, and responsible theological inference.
Students investigate Jesus, the cross, resurrection, conversion, baptism, grace, obedience, and perseverance with explicit separation of text and synthesis.
Students examine the church Jesus established, its worship and leadership, and its mission while distinguishing explicit text, pattern, and inference.
Students test Christian claims and ethics against difficult evidence, rival worldviews, contemporary pressures, and pastoral realities.
Students trace Christianity from Acts to the present, evaluate continuity claims, study eschatological hope, and build an independent method of faithful study and participation.

decision_register.framework_position: Canonical Scripture is the primary and final doctrinal authority for the curriculum.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Traditions that give binding doctrinal authority to church tradition or an ongoing teaching office.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: How Scripture describes its authority and how canonical synthesis is formed.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach confidence in Scripture without pretending interpretation is automatic.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not equate a teacher interpretation with the words of the text.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Targeted bibliology packet on canon, inspiration, and interpretation.

decision_register.framework_position: Use the 66-book Protestant canon as the operative curriculum canon.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Catholic and Orthodox canons include additional books with differing levels of authority.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: The distinction between the Hebrew canon, Septuagint collections, later canon lists, and ecclesial reception.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach the 66-book structure; introduce canon history later.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not claim the table of contents dropped from heaven or that canon history is simple.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Primary-source canon history packet.

decision_register.issue: Use of Apocrypha, Septuagint, and other ancient sources
decision_register.framework_position: Noncanonical ancient sources may illuminate language, history, textual traditions, and Second Temple context but do not independently establish doctrine.
decision_register.key_passages: Daniel 2; Luke 1:1-4; Jude 14-15 as contextual discussion points
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Traditions that recognise some or all Deuterocanonical books as Scripture.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: Whether a source is being used as evidence of context, reception, or binding doctrine.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Use context selectively and label it clearly.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not call a historical source Scripture within this curriculum.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Source-by-source reliability and scope review.
decision_register.decision_note: Approved as written.

decision_register.framework_position: Jesus established and owns His church; Acts describes its apostolic public formation and mission.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: No serious Christian alternative denies Christ as founder, though traditions differ on institutional continuity and authority.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: Distinguishing theological foundation from later institutional succession claims.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach that the church belongs to Jesus and follows His teaching.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not imply that the church began in the Reformation or nineteenth century.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Church continuity and institutional history packet.

decision_register.issue: New Testament as normative pattern for church belief and practice
decision_register.framework_position: The New Testament supplies the normative apostolic basis for Christian doctrine, worship, organisation, and mission. Its pattern is discerned through explicit command, approved apostolic example, and necessary inference, read with attention to genre, context, and canonical coherence.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Traditions integrate Scripture with binding post-apostolic tradition or a continuing magisterium.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: How commands, approved examples, necessary inference, genre, local circumstances, and canonical coherence function normatively.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach command, approved example, and necessary inference progressively, and label the evidence type behind each conclusion.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not treat every narrative detail as a universal law or every human inference as equal to an explicit command.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Hermeneutics packet on command, example, inference, and canonical synthesis.
decision_register.decision_note: Approved. The New Testament pattern is discerned through command, approved example, and necessary inference.

decision_register.issue: Identity, lordship, death, and resurrection of Jesus
decision_register.framework_position: Jesus is the Messiah and Son of God, truly human, crucified, bodily raised, exalted, and reigning as Lord.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Nontrinitarian and nonresurrection interpretations dispute one or more elements.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: The relation of direct texts, titles, worship, agency, and later theological terminology.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach the biblical claims before technical terminology.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not rely on a later creed as the sole basis of the doctrine.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Christology packet including major alternative readings.

decision_register.framework_position: The New Testament presents hearing the gospel, faith, repentance, confession, baptism, forgiveness, reception of new life, and continuing discipleship as an integrated response.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Many evangelicals place justification before baptism and treat baptism as a subsequent sign.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: How conversion narratives and doctrinal passages relate; the timing and function of baptism.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Introduce baptism without pressure; teach full conversion narratives rather than a mechanical checklist.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not describe baptism as a human work that earns salvation or judge every exceptional case.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Full baptism and conversion evidence packet.

decision_register.framework_position: Immersion in water is the normative mode represented by the New Testament language and imagery.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Other traditions accept pouring or sprinkling based on lexical range, early practice, or pastoral circumstance.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: Lexical evidence, narrative description, burial imagery, and early historical practice.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Describe baptism as immersion in water.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not claim every historical baptism used identical physical circumstances.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Greek lexical and early-practice packet.

decision_register.framework_position: Baptism is associated with personal hearing, faith, repentance, and response; infant baptism is not treated as the normative New Testament pattern.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Paedobaptist traditions appeal to covenant continuity and household baptisms.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: The relationship between covenant households, silence about infants, and explicit believer-response texts.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: State positively that baptism belongs to a person able to believe and repent.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not mock or caricature paedobaptist families.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Paedobaptist covenant argument packet.

decision_register.framework_position: No child should be pressured toward baptism to please adults, belong socially, or complete a curriculum milestone.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Some congregations use fixed ages or simplified readiness tests.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: How understanding, voluntariness, repentance, family influence, and pastoral care are assessed.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach meaning and invite questions; route personal readiness through a separate pastoral process.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not include conversion pressure, public comparison, or gamified baptism prompts.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Create a child-safe baptism conversation protocol.
decision_register.decision_note: Approved. A separate child-safe baptism-readiness protocol remains required before publication. Deferred by the project owner on 2026-08-12 for separate completion. The existing child-facing rule and prohibited-overstatement guardrails remain active, but the research or pastoral protocol is not a blocker for schema validation or non-sensitive vertical-slice development.
decision_register.workflow_disposition: Deferred - owner-managed outside current build stream

decision_register.framework_position: The Supper remembers and proclaims Jesus, expresses participation and unity, calls for self-examination, and anticipates His return.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Christian traditions differ over presence, sacrifice, memorial, and sacramental efficacy.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: How the institution narratives and Pauline language are synthesised.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach remembrance, proclamation, unity, gratitude, and hope.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not reduce the Supper to a snack or force children into adult sacramental disputes.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Lord’s Supper exegesis and history packet.
decision_register.decision_note: Approved as written.

decision_register.framework_position: The congregation observes the Supper every first day of the week as the best reading of apostolic practice.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Other Christians see frequency as flexible because no text directly states a universal weekly command.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: Whether Acts 20:7 establishes a recurring normative pattern and how first-day gatherings relate to frequency.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach the local practice and later show the inference behind it.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not say Acts 20:7 explicitly commands every congregation to commune weekly.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Frequency and first-day practice packet.
decision_register.decision_note: Approved as written.

decision_register.framework_position: The congregation uses unleavened bread and grape juice as bread and fruit of the vine connected to Passover and its own practice.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Many Christians use leavened bread, wine, or other contextually available elements.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: What is explicit in the texts, Passover context, historical practice, and prudential substitution.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Describe the congregation’s elements without making unsupported universal claims.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not claim the New Testament directly uses the term grape juice.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Historical and lexical elements packet.
decision_register.decision_note: Approved as written.

decision_register.framework_position: The congregation practises unaccompanied congregational singing because vocal singing is the positive New Testament pattern it sees authorised.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Other Christians view instruments as a permissible aid because they are not prohibited and appear in biblical worship elsewhere.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: The force of positive pattern, silence, psallo, covenant continuity, and historical practice.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach joyful vocal participation first; teach the hermeneutical case later.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not claim users of instruments are automatically condemned or that early evidence is unanimous.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Psallo, silence, covenant, and early worship packet.
decision_register.decision_note: Approved as written.

decision_register.issue: Equal dignity of women and men
decision_register.framework_position: Women and men bear God’s image, share salvation and inheritance in Christ, and perform significant service in Scripture.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: No mainstream Christian alternative denies equal dignity, though role conclusions differ.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: How equality, gifts, service, and role texts relate.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Include substantial examples of faithful women and men.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not equate role distinction with inferior worth.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Canonical women-in-Scripture coverage audit.

decision_register.framework_position: The office of elder or overseer is reserved for qualified men based on the stated qualifications and wider framework.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Egalitarian interpretations read the qualifications as culturally expressed character requirements rather than a permanent sex restriction.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: The significance of husband-language, household leadership, creation arguments, and evidence of women in leadership.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Kids learn caring qualified leaders; full argument is reserved for Teens.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not teach that every adult male is qualified or that women lack leadership capacity.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Eldership qualifications and egalitarian response packet.

decision_register.issue: Women and assembly preaching or teaching over men
decision_register.framework_position: In the assembled congregation women do not occupy the preaching or authoritative teaching role over men, while serving broadly in other contexts.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Egalitarian interpretations read restrictions as local responses to disorder or false teaching.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: Creation appeal, local context, meaning of teach and authority, and reconciliation with women praying or prophesying.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Delay detailed dispute; state local practice without diminishing women’s service.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not erase prophetesses, Priscilla, Phoebe, or other female co-workers.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Exegetical packet on 1 Timothy 2 and 1 Corinthians 11 and 14.
decision_register.decision_note: Approved as written.

decision_register.framework_position: The curriculum teaches the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit from Scripture. The term Trinity may be used as a concise later summary of that biblical teaching, but it does not function as an independent authority or make a later creed the foundation of doctrine.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Nontrinitarian readings dispute the later synthesis or terminology.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: How later technical terminology can accurately summarize the biblical evidence without replacing Scripture as the authority.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach the biblical persons and relationships first; introduce the term Trinity only after that concrete biblical foundation is established.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not imply that the word Trinity appears in Scripture or that Nicene wording is the doctrinal foundation of the curriculum.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Biblical doctrine of God packet independent of creedal authority.
decision_register.decision_note: Approved use of Trinitarian terminology, with Scripture rather than a later creed remaining the doctrinal foundation.

decision_register.framework_position: Salvation, reconciliation, and atonement are in Christ alone. The curriculum teaches the biblical descriptions of His work - sacrifice, substitution, redemption, reconciliation, justification, victory, and covenant - as complementary, without making one later model an exhaustive account of the cross.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Penal substitution, Christus Victor, participation, sacrifice, moral influence, and other models emphasise different texts.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: How the biblical images relate while maintaining Christ alone as the complete and sufficient basis of salvation.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach that Jesus alone saves and use the biblical images appropriate to the passage; reserve comparison of named atonement models for Teens.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not imply that salvation comes through any person, institution, or human merit, and do not make one later model the only biblical description of Christ's work.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Atonement models evidence packet.
decision_register.decision_note: Approved with the controlling principle that salvation and atonement are in Christ alone.

decision_register.framework_position: All morally accountable people sin and therefore deserve death. Accountability presupposes the capacity to recognize sin and make a meaningful moral response; infants, children who have not reached that capacity, and persons whose mental capacity prevents such recognition are not held personally accountable for sin they cannot understand.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Augustinian and Reformed accounts teach inherited guilt or condemnation from Adam, while other traditions distinguish inherited mortality or corruption from personal guilt.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: The relationship between Adamic death, inherited consequences, personal guilt, knowledge, capacity, and individual responsibility.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach sin as a personally accountable choice once a person can understand right, wrong, and repentance; never tell a young child or person lacking capacity that they are personally condemned.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not assign one fixed chronological age of accountability to every person or teach that infants and people lacking relevant capacity bear personal guilt.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Passage-level packet on Romans 5, Ezekiel 18, moral knowledge, and accountability; develop a capacity-sensitive pastoral explanation rather than a fixed-age rule.
decision_register.decision_note: Teach that morally accountable persons sin and deserve death; children and persons lacking capacity are not accountable until capable of recognizing sin.

decision_register.framework_position: The miraculous revelatory and sign gifts recorded in the New Testament served to confirm Jesus, the apostles, and the proclaimed word. That confirming work has been completed; no person possesses those miraculous gifts today.
decision_register.key_passages: Mark 16:17-20; Acts 8:14-19; 1 Corinthians 12-14; 2 Corinthians 12:12; Hebrews 2:3-4; Ephesians 4:11-16
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Continuationist traditions hold that prophecy, tongues, healing, and other miraculous gifts continue in the church today.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: The confirming purpose of signs, the relation of gifts to apostles and revelation, the meaning of maturity or completion texts, and the evidential standard for present claims.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach the New Testament miracles and gifts in their historical purpose; explain the present cessation conclusion only with age-appropriate textual reasoning.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not imply that God is powerless, that prayer is ineffective, or that providence has ceased; distinguish God's action from a person possessing an apostolic miraculous gift.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Cessation evidence packet covering confirming signs, apostolic mediation, 1 Corinthians 13, Ephesians 4, and the strongest continuationist case.
decision_register.decision_note: Teach that miraculous gifts confirmed Jesus, the apostles, and the word; that confirming purpose is complete and no person possesses those miraculous gifts today.

decision_register.framework_position: The curriculum affirms divine sovereignty, genuine human response, and universal gospel proclamation. Christ's saving work has been completed fully and is wholly sufficient; human response receives that work and does not add merit or completeness to it.
decision_register.key_passages: John 19:30; Romans 8-9; Ephesians 1; Hebrews 10:10-14; 1 Timothy 2:1-6; 2 Peter 3:9; Acts 17:30
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Calvinist, Arminian, corporate-election, and other accounts differ.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: How divine initiative and sovereignty relate to a genuine, accountable human response and the universal call of the gospel.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach that God acts first and completely in Christ, the gospel is for all, and each hearer is genuinely called to respond in faith and obedience.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not teach that human response earns salvation, that Christ's work needs supplementation, or that divine sovereignty makes the gospel invitation unreal.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Passage-level election and response packet; avoid forcing the curriculum into Calvinist or Arminian system labels where the approved formulation is sufficient.
decision_register.decision_note: Affirm divine sovereignty, genuine human response, universal gospel proclamation, and the complete and sufficient work of Christ.

decision_register.framework_position: Christ's sacrifice removed the barrier of sin and opened the way to eternal life. Each Christian must continue faithfully, run the race set before them, and remain on the narrow way; a Christian can fall away and lose the promised eternal rest.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Perseverance-of-the-saints and eternal-security traditions hold that a truly regenerated person cannot finally lose salvation.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: Whether the warning recipients are genuine Christians, what falling away entails, and how assurance promises relate to conditional warnings.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach confidence in Christ together with the real call to remain faithful; use race, path, and perseverance language without creating constant fear.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not teach that one mistake instantly removes salvation, that assurance is impossible, or that warnings to Christians are hypothetical and meaningless.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Conditional-security packet covering assurance texts and the warning passages in Hebrews, 2 Peter, and Revelation.
decision_register.decision_note: Teach that Christ opened the way to eternal life, but each Christian must continue faithfully; a Christian can fall away and lose eternal rest.

decision_register.framework_position: The curriculum teaches final accountability and two ultimate outcomes at judgment: going home to life with God in heaven or going to hell, understood as separation from God. Christ is victorious, and every person is accountable to Him.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Conditional-immortality, universalist, and differing eternal-punishment accounts interpret the nature, duration, and imagery of final punishment differently.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: How eternal life, death, destruction, exclusion, separation, and apocalyptic imagery are related in canonical synthesis.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach judgment soberly and age-appropriately as the final distinction between life with God and separation from Him, always within the gospel invitation.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not use graphic fear, speculative geography, or invented details to manipulate children or claim certainty beyond the approved biblical formulation.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Passage-level final-judgment packet to standardize vocabulary for heaven, hell, separation, death, destruction, and eternal punishment.
decision_register.decision_note: Teach final judgment with two outcomes: home with God in heaven or hell, understood as separation from God.

decision_register.framework_position: The curriculum teaches the resurrection of the dead, Christ's return, final judgment, and the new spiritual creation. No premillennial, postmillennial, or amillennial timetable is made a required doctrine of the curriculum.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Premillennial, postmillennial, and amillennial readings differ.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: How apocalyptic genre, chronology, resurrection, judgment, and new-creation language relate without making a speculative timeline controlling.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Emphasise Christ's return, resurrection, judgment, and the promised new spiritual creation; reserve comparison of millennial systems for older Teens.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not set dates, turn symbolic texts into a rigid chart, or require one millennial system as a test of salvation or fellowship.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Eschatology language packet focused on resurrection, return, judgment, and new creation, with millennial models treated comparatively rather than normatively.
decision_register.decision_note: Teach resurrection, Christ's return, judgment, and the new spiritual creation without requiring a millennial system.

decision_register.framework_position: The curriculum affirms God as Creator, creation's goodness, human image-bearing, and moral accountability. Interpretations of the creation days, chronology, and mechanisms may be compared, but those disputes have no material bearing on salvation and are not tests of fellowship.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Young-earth, old-earth, evolutionary creation, and literary-framework views differ.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: Genre, the sequence of the creation account including the fourth-day lights, genealogies, death before the fall, scientific evidence, and the distinction between core doctrine and non-salvific models.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach God as Creator and the theological meaning of Genesis; compare chronology and mechanism models only in Teens and explicitly state that the debate is not a salvation test.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not present one scientific or chronological model as a direct quotation from Genesis or question a student's salvation because of a model held in good faith.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Creation models packet using scientific and exegetical primary sources, framed as a non-salvific interpretive question.
decision_register.decision_note: The dispute over creation chronology and mechanisms is not material to salvation and must not become a salvation or fellowship test.

decision_register.framework_position: The curriculum teaches enemy love, refusal of personal vengeance, and primary allegiance to Christ. Christians respect rulers and laws unless obedience would violate God's law. Military service may be morally justified where its purpose and conduct are lawful, protect people, uphold just order, and remain subordinate to God's commands.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Historic Christian pacifism holds that discipleship prohibits participation in lethal force; just-war traditions permit force only under stringent moral conditions.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: The relation of enemy love to government, protection of neighbour, obedience to rulers, conscience, lawful authority, and refusal of commands contrary to God.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach nonvengeance and respect for authority first; older Teens may compare pacifist and just-war reasoning and examine military service as a morally accountable vocation.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not treat legality alone as moral permission, automatically bless every war or military order, condemn conscientious pacifists, or equate nationalism with Christian faithfulness.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: War, military service, conscience, and lawful-authority packet including early Christian practice and the strongest pacifist and just-war arguments.
decision_register.decision_note: Teach enemy love and no personal vengeance; obey rulers unless their commands violate God's law; military service may be justified when lawful, protective, and consistent with God's law.

decision_register.framework_position: Marriage is a covenant intended for faithfulness; disputed cases of divorce and remarriage require exegetical and pastoral protocols.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Strict exception, broader exception, abandonment, abuse, and penitential approaches differ.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: Meaning of exception clauses, porneia, abandonment, safety, repentance, and restoration.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach the ideal and safety; route personal cases away from group debate.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not use classroom content to adjudicate a family’s case or keep someone in danger.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Exegetical and safeguarding protocol.

decision_register.issue: Church continuity from AD 33 to today
decision_register.framework_position: Christ’s church did not begin in the Reformation or Restoration Movement; claims of institutional and doctrinal continuity must be distinguished and evidenced.
decision_register.key_passages: Matthew 16:18; Ephesians 3:20-21; 2 Timothy 2:1-2; selected historical sources
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Catholic, Orthodox, Protestant, restorationist, and invisible-church models make different continuity claims.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: Difference between theological continuity, institutional succession, doctrinal fidelity, and recurrent restoration.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Teach continuous Christian history without a disappearance myth or automatic succession argument.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not claim an institution is correct merely because it is old, or that all faithful Christians vanished.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: AD 33-to-present primary-source history packet.

decision_register.framework_position: The curriculum teaches God's design of male and female and the marriage and family structure presented in Scripture, while preserving the dignity and safety of every student. Pastoral care must not compromise the approved biblical ethic, and the curriculum must not treat children from different or disrupted family circumstances as lesser.
decision_register.strongest_credible_alternative: Affirming Christian and secular accounts interpret the texts and human identity differently.
decision_register.interpretive_hinge: Exegesis, embodiment, desire, identity, pastoral care, and the difference between persons and propositions.
decision_register.child_facing_rule: Use age-appropriate language, teach the approved biblical design positively, avoid public disclosure pressure, protect students from contempt, and provide clear safeguarding routes.
decision_register.prohibited_overstatement: Do not compromise the approved biblical family ethic, and do not use contempt, slurs, pseudo-scientific claims, public interrogation, or language that shames a child for their family circumstances.
decision_register.targeted_research_need: Sexual ethics, gender, and pastoral-care protocol.
